source: OBR, Economic and fiscal outlook, October 2026, Annex A
replaces: OBR EFO March 2026, as shipped in policyengine-uk 2.151.0 (gov.economic_assumptions.yoy_growth.obr)
applies_to: Every simulation the dashboard builds, baseline and reform alike (uk_budget_data.forecast.with_forecast). Applied before data load, so the dataset's projected years follow it.
notes: Growth rates are Table A.1 (Economy forecast, EFO page 180), percentage change on a year earlier, calendar years 2026 to 2031, keyed YYYY-01-01.YYYY-12-31. 2025 is outturn in Table A.1 and is left as shipped; after 2031 the engine's long-run path is kept.
The engine's March values equal the March Table A.1 rows: the October value minus the Table A.2 change since March, to within 0.1pp rounding (tests/test_forecast_basis.py).

Statutory uprating inputs keep their published outturns (September 2026 CPI 3.5%, May-July 2026 earnings 3.9%). Their forecast years are calendar-year growth plus the engine's forecast_gap, which still holds the March 2026 quarterly gaps except where noted below.

September 2027 CPI: Table A.3 (EFO page 181) gives the 2027-28 triple-lock guarantee as 3.4%, the highest of Q2 2027 earnings growth, Q3 2027 CPI and 2.5%. Q2 earnings cannot reach 3.4% (calendar-year 2027 earnings growth is 3.0%), so Q3 2027 CPI is 3.4%, equal to calendar-year 2027 CPI: the gap is 0. The March gap (+0.07pp) would have given 3.5%.
Every later Table A.3 triple-lock figure (2.5, 2.5, 2.5, 2.6 for 2028-29 to 2031-32) is reproduced by these series and the remaining March gaps (tests/test_forecast_basis.py).

Fuel duty (gov.hmrc.fuel_duty.petrol_and_diesel), added in code (uk_budget_data.forecast.fuel_duty_rpi_steps): policyengine-uk stores current law's RPI steps as values from its March RPI. Current law here is the OBR's 60.59p from April 2027 (EFO paragraph 3.19: on 1 July 2027 the 5p cut is reversed with an RPI uprating, 52.95p to 60.59p; the Budget defers that same planned RPI increase from April), then each 1 April the previous calendar year's Table A.1 RPI. The baseline and the fuel duty measure both read this one path.

Not updated (the OBR detailed forecast tables could not be retrieved): cpih, non_labour_income, rent, mortgage_interest, per_capita, council_tax, fuel volume and price series. They keep the March 2026 path. consumer_price_index_ahc and social_rent are derived from Table A.1 CPI (see their sources).

gov.economic_assumptions.yoy_growth.obr..source: Table A.1, Labour market: Average weekly earnings (wages and salaries divided by employees)
Table A.1, Household sector: House prices

Table A.1, CPI, as a change: PolicyEngine approximation (not an OBR series), policyengine-uk's March 2026 CPI after housing costs moved by the change in Table A.1 CPI for the same year, as the Living standards tab's October series (living_standards/forecast.py)
Table A.1, CPI: England social rent policy cap, the previous calendar year's CPI + 1% (2026 is set by September 2025 CPI outturn and kept), as the Living standards tab's October series

gov.economic_assumptions.statutory_uprat.source: Table A.3, 'Triple-lock' guarantee 2027-28: 3.4 (Q3 2027 CPI) minus Table A.1 calendar-year 2027 CPI 3.4
